title: Validation - Senior Director, Process & Cleaning Validation
description:
When joining PerkinElmer, you select an experienced and trusted leader in scientific solutions, with the support of a global service network and distribution centers, providing the right solution, at the right time, to meet critical customer needs. With over an 80+ year legacy of advancing science and a mission of innovating for a healthier world, our dedicated team collaborates closely with commercial, government, academic and healthcare customers to deliver our broad portfolio of analytical solutions, and OneSource services.

Job Title

Validation - Senior Director, Process & Cleaning Validation


Location(s)

Customer Site - IN

Job Description

This is a full-time salaried position with Project Farma, a PerkinElmer company. The successful candidate will be willing to travel domestically and internationally, to meet client project requests.

Project Farma’s purpose is to improve patient lives by accelerating the delivery of life-changing therapies. We accomplish this through the successful execution of high-quality life sciences projects across the full project lifecycle. Project Farma (PF) team members collaborate with cross-functional teams to build trusted client relationships, deliver an exceptional customer experience, and contribute to business growth by identifying opportunities and applying data-driven insights to support project planning, cost, schedule, and performance management.

All team members are expected to embody Project Farma’s values by being curious, personable, and unselfish, while maintaining a strong commitment to a Patient Focused and People First mindset.

The Senior Director, Process & Cleaning Validation Services is a senior leader responsible for setting direction, driving execution, and delivering results across the Validation Services Practice Area, with a technical focus on process validation, cleaning and sterilization validation, and holistic validation lifecycle programs. This role provides strategic leadership, oversees multiple project teams or initiatives, and partners cross-functionally to align people, processes, and priorities with the company objectives. This role carries enterprise-level accountability for strategic direction, leadership development, and sustained business performance across a significant organizational scope. The incumbent shapes and influences decisions at scale, ensures operational excellence, and builds leadership capability — balancing near-term execution priorities with long-term growth objectives.

Key Responsibilities

Practice Leadership & Standardization

  • Define and maintain standardized approaches, templates, and SOPs for process validation and cleaning and sterilization validation across the organization
  • Ensure alignment with current regulatory frameworks including FDA Process Validation Guidance, ICH Q7/Q8/Q9, Annex 1, and other relevant guidance
  • Champion holistic validation lifecycle approaches, integrating process design, qualification, and continued process verification (CPV) stages
  • Serve as the internal authority on process and cleaning validation strategy, methodology, and regulatory expectations
  • Monitor industry trends, guidance updates, and emerging science to keep the practice current and competitive . Share this knowledge and insight with clients and the greater industry as an ongoing business practice.

Training & Knowledge Development

  • Develop and maintain a current comprehensive training curriculum covering process validation lifecycle stages, cleaning validation principles, and applicable regulatory standards
  • Drive consistent technical competency across staff through onboarding programs, ongoing training, and formal assessments
  • Create and manage a library of training resources, case studies, and reference materials to support continuous learning related to process, cleaning and sterilization validation principles.
  • Identify knowledge gaps and proactively design content to address evolving regulatory and industry requirements

Innovation & Lifecycle Modernization

  • Lead adoption of modern lifecycle-based validation approaches integrating continued process verification (CPV) and statistical process control (SPC)
  • Respond to growing industry demand for holistic validation lifecycle programs as pharma companies embrace more integrated approaches to process and cleaning validation
  • Develop risk-based frameworks that align validation rigor with product and process criticality
  • Evaluate and implement emerging technologies and data analytics tools to enhance validation program effectiveness and efficiency

Business Growth & Development

  • Support growth of the Process & Cleaning Validation service line by identifying and pursuing new client opportunities
  • Contribute to proposals, scope development, and client presentations to expand the practice revenue base
  • Build and maintain strong client relationships, acting as a trusted technical advisor on validation strategy and regulatory compliance
  • Collaborate with business development and other practice leaders to identify cross-sell opportunities across service lines
  • Maintain business development activity and pipeline data within the firm's customer relationship management (CRM) system
  • Speak at multiple industry events and publish insights in reputable publications

Leadership & Talent Development

  • Provide technical mentorship and career development guidance to consultant staff within the P&CV practice
  • Support talent acquisition by identifying staffing needs, participating in interviews, and onboarding new team members
  • Foster a culture of technical excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement within the team
  • Contribute to performance management processes and provide input on staff development plans

Technical Delivery

  • Provide technical oversight and quality review on P&CV project deliverables including validation plans, protocols, reports, and risk assessments
  • Ensure deliverables meet client requirements, Project Farma standards, and applicable regulatory expectations
  • Serve as subject matter expert and escalation point for complex technical challenges across active projects
  • Maintain direct engagement on key accounts to ensure technical quality and client satisfaction

Operational Performance & Billability

  • Maintain a level of individual billability through direct client delivery while concurrently leading practice-level responsibilities
  • Track and report on practice-level metrics including project performance, utilization, and delivery quality
  • Support resource planning and allocation decisions to optimize team productivity and client service
  • Identify and escalate operational risks that may impact project timelines, scope, or quality

Attributes for Success

  • Technical Delivery: Applies advanced technical knowledge and professional expertise
  • Innovation & Continuous Improvement: Seeks better ways, adapts to change and champions new ideas.
  • Customer Focus & Professionalism: Represents PF with consistent professionalism, appropriate escalation and respect for internal stakeholders, even during high stress delivery situations
  • Integrity & Humility: Demonstrates self-awareness and puts PF mission above ego
  • Collaboration & Communication: Communicates clearly and proactively and drives transparent alignment with clients.
  • Project Execution: Delivers reliably, manages priorities and drives for high quality outcomes
  • Growth Mindset: Shows openness to new ideas, feedback and change

Experience Required

  • Bachelor’s Degree (and/or Masters) in Life Science, Engineering, or related discipline (OR a combination of equivalent experience in CQV engineering, cGMP facility start-up, project management and/or comparable military experience)
  • 15+ years advanced therapy, life science, pharmaceutical, or biotech experience
  • 10 years minimum managing high-performing teams
  • 6 years minimum business development, lead generation, or sales experience

Other Required

  • Travel as needed to fulfill Business Development, client engagement and training initiatives.
  • Experience operating as a trusted strategic advisor to organization decision-makers on short and long-term organizational initiatives.
  • Experience translating client visions to set the direction, frame the project, provide clarity to direct reports and client, and deliver results
  • Proven technical/managerial capabilities in developing solutions to engineering and business problems and managing deliverables and client expectations

title: Retail Sale Associate - Stonestown Galleria (SF)
description:
POP MART (09992.HK), founded in 2010, is a leading global company in the trend culture and entertainment industry. Centered around IP, POP MART has built a comprehensive platform for creative incubation and IP operation, empowering global creators while delivering exciting products, services, and immersive entertainment experiences to consumers.

POP MART identifies and nurtures emerging artists and designers worldwide, creating popular character IPs through a well-established IP development and operation system. Its portfolio includes iconic IPs such as MOLLY, SKULLPANDA, DIMOO, THE MONSTERS, and Hirono. By launching art toys and derivative products based on these IPs, POP MART continues to lead trends in consumer culture. As of the end of first half of 2025, POP MART operates over 550 physical stores and more than 2,500 Robo Shops across the world. Through multiple cross-border e-commerce platforms, the company has reached audiences in over 90 countries and regions, bringing joy to young consumers around the world.





Job Overview

POP MART is seeking energetic, customer-focused Sales Associates who are passionate about creating memorable shopping experiences and bringing our unique brand to life. As a Sales Associate, you will serve as a brand ambassador by delivering exceptional service, building genuine connections with customers, and helping drive store performance through product knowledge, storytelling, and sales excellence.
In this role, you will create an engaging in-store experience by understanding each customer's needs, introducing them to POP MART's world of collectible art toys, and providing personalized recommendations that inspire excitement and repeat visits. You will also support daily store operations including merchandising, inventory management, and maintaining a clean, organized, and welcoming environment.
A passion for designer toys, collectibles, art, fashion, anime, gaming, or pop culture is highly valued and will help you succeed in this role.

What You Will Achieve

  • Deliver an exceptional customer experience by warmly welcoming every guest and building authentic customer relationships.
  • Become a brand ambassador by confidently sharing POP MART's story, artist collaborations, collectible characters, product collections, promotions, and membership program.
  • Educate customers on our collectible culture, including Blind Boxes, MEGA Collections, accessories, limited editions, and new product launches.
  • Drive sales by identifying customer needs, making personalized product recommendations, upselling complementary merchandise, and achieving individual and store sales goals.
  • Accurately process customer purchases, returns, exchanges, and loyalty transactions using the point-of-sale system.
  • Assist with receiving shipments, replenishing merchandise, organizing inventory, and maintaining stockroom accuracy.
  • Maintain exceptional store presentation by ensuring cleanliness, organization, and safety throughout the sales floor and backroom.
  • Support inventory accuracy through cycle counts, stock replenishment, and operational best practices.
  • Collaborate with teammates to achieve daily sales goals, operational objectives, and an outstanding customer experience.
  • Cross-train to support POP MART Robo Shop (vending machine) replenishment and inventory processes as business needs require.
  • Maintain compliance with company policies, cash handling procedures, and loss prevention standards.

What You Will Need

  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred.
  • 1+ year of customer-facing retail, hospitality, entertainment, or service industry experience preferred.
  • Passion for delivering exceptional customer service and creating memorable experiences.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to engage customers from diverse backgrounds.
  • Ability to build rapport quickly and confidently recommend products.

title: Librarian I - Joel D. Valdez Main Library
description:
Job Description Summary

Department - County Free Library

Job Description

OPEN TO CURRENT PIMA COUNTY EMPLOYEES ONLY

Job Type: Classified

Job Classification: 5654 - Librarian I

Salary Grade: 10

Pay Range

Hiring Range: $53,872 - $64,625 Annually

Pay Range: $53, 872 - $75,379 Annually

Range Explanation:

  • Hiring Range is an estimate of where you can receive an offer. The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, education, licenses, training, and internal equity.

  • Pay Range is the entire compensation range for the position.

The Pima County Public Library is seeking an experienced Librarian I at the Joel D. Valdez Main Library to join its Circulations Services team! We are looking for a candidate who is passionate about providing outstanding customer service and supporting a welcoming library environment. The ideal candidate has strong knowledge of circulation services, Sierra ILS, and systemwide circulation procedures, experience supervising staff in a public library, and a commitment to improving library services through collaboration, innovation, and project implementation. Candidates should be organized, able to manage multiple priorities, work effectively both independently and as part of a team, and demonstrate excellent communication skills.

This position requires the ability to report to, and travel between, assigned library locations during the workday within a reasonable timeframe.

Essential Functions:

As defined under the Americans with Disabilities Act, this classification may include any of the following tasks, knowledge, skills, and other characteristics. This list is ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY and is not a comprehensive listing of all functions and tasks performed by incumbents of this class. Work assignments may vary depending on the department’s need and will be communicated to the applicant or incumbent by the supervisor.

  • Oversees assigned service area within a library such as youth services or adult services by developing, presenting, and coordinating services inclusive of all members of the public including vulnerable populations;

  • Serves as supervisor in charge of the library as assigned;

  • Assists members of the public by finding and relaying library and community resource information including providing assistance in using the library’s collections, catalog, technology, and equipment;

  • Develops, facilitates, and/or presents evidence-based educational programs and services, including early literacy programs, community outreach activities, youth advisory boards, and computer and technology instruction in person or virtually;

  • Supervises library employees, volunteers, and/or interns by training, scheduling, and evaluating performance, making recommendations regarding probationary periods, employee discipline, and other human resources-related matters;

  • Incorporates and implements public service best practices, including culturally competent community-driven programming, public relations, problem solving, conflict management and complaint resolution;

  • Utilizes conflict management skills to de-escalate and address unexpected problems or potentially volatile situations and complete associated documentation;

  • Performs facilities management duties by monitoring and reporting maintenance issues and investigating or resolving operational or technical issues;

  • Participates in or facilitates systemwide committee meetings focused on youth services, adult services, library strategic directions or core values and attend relevant continuing education trainings and workshops to incorporate current best practices in a particular service level;

  • Manages, coordinates, and determines priorities of workload, including monitoring levels of resources, establishing timelines, assigning work, monitoring progress, recommending changes and suggestions, writing, reviewing, and editing reports prepared by staff.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with a major in Library Science, Liberal Arts, Social Science, Information Management, Business Administration, Public Administration or a related field as determined by the department head at the time of recruitment AND three years of experience in libraries, customer service, education, social services or fields of similar scope.

(Relevant experience and/or education from an accredited college or university may be substituted.)

Qualifying education and experience must be clearly documented in the "Education" and "Work Experience" sections of the application. Do not substitute a resume for your application or write "see resume" on your application.

Preferred Qualifications: (Be specific in describing your experience in your application. Ensure the descriptions provided illustrate your competencies, specifically addressing the required and preferred qualifications.):

  • Minimum two (2) years experience with circulation policies, procedures, and working knowledge of Sierra (ILS) functions.

  • Minimum two (2) years experience supervising staff in a public library setting.

  • Master's degree in library and information science (MLIS) from an ALA-accredited program.

  • Experience leading or participating in projects that improve library services or operations.

  • Experience prioritizing multiple tasks while staying organized within timeframes.

  • Experience working collaboratively as part of a team while also exercising sound independent judgment.

  • Bilingual (English/Spanish - speaking, reading, writing).

​

Selection Procedure:
Pima County Human Resources Department reserves the right to admit to the selection process only those candidates that meet the minimum qualifications. All applications will be assessed based on an evaluation of the listed education and experience. Candidates meeting the minimum qualifications may be further evaluated/scored against any advertised Preferred Qualifications. The hiring authority will interview and select the successful candidate from a referral list provided by Human Resources. Additional assessments/testing may be required as part of the selection process.

Supplemental Information:

Licenses and Certificates: Some positions may require specialized certification or licensure relative to assignment at the time of appointment or prior to completion of an initial or promotional probation period. Some positions require a valid Arizona Class D driver license at the time of application or prior to completion of an initial or promotional probation period. Failure to obtain/maintain the required certifications/licenses shall be grounds for termination.

Special Notice Items: The County requires pre-employment background checks. Successful candidates will receive a post-offer, pre-employment background screening to include verification of work history, education, and criminal conviction history. A prior criminal conviction will not automatically disqualify a candidate from employment with the County. This position works rotating shifts, including nights and weekends. Some positions may require bilingual abilities in English and a second language, as determined by the department head.

Physical/Sensory Requirements: Physical and sensory abilities will be determined by position. Action Activity - squatting; Motion Activity - grasping; Speaking Activity - in person and on the phone; Vision - ability to distinguish colors.

Working Conditions: Primarily works in a public Library environment serving diverse populations. Other working conditions will be determined by position.

EEO Information: Pima County Government is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We are committed to an inclusive and diverse workforce and will not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, gender, sexual orientation, kinship, political interest, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Stagiair Adviseur Vermogen regio Den Haag
description:
Stagiair Adviseur Vermogen

Heeft beleggen jouw interesse? En sta je open voor een carrière binnen de financiële sector? Deze meewerkstage voor de periode vanaf februari 2027 betekent dat je onder begeleiding van een persoonlijke coach binnen Adviesteam Vermogen in- en outbound werkzaamheden verricht die een Adviseur Vermogen dagelijks doet. Afgestemd op jouw kennis en ervaring doorloop je, samen met maximaal drie andere stagiaires, een leertraject en ga je aan de slag met het (verder) ontwikkelen van jouw gespreksvaardigheden, sales skills en het behalen van de benodigde vakdiploma’s. Het doel is om je zelfstandig, op een ING locatie en digitaal (vanuit huis), te laten werken en dagelijks contact te laten hebben met particuliere- en zakelijke klanten over beleggen bij ING.

Leertraject fase 1:

  • Je start tegelijkertijd met maximaal vier stagiaires en komt te werken binnen het Digitaal Vermogen Team (DVT). Een groot team van adviseurs die het 1e aanspreekpunt zijn voor bestaande klanten in het ‘Guided model’ (belegd vermogen van € 50.000 tot € 500.000) én verantwoordelijk zijn voor de centrale leadgeneratie vanuit outbound-, inbound- en online activiteiten richting de commerciële teams van Adviesteam Vermogen en Private Banking.
  • Je gaat onder begeleiding van een persoonlijke coach vrijwel direct starten met klantcontact via outbound bellen om je gespreksvaardigheden ‘on the job’ te ontwikkelen en de Way of Working te leren. Indien nodig behaal je onder werktijd de benodigde vakdiploma’s waardoor je meer verschillende type klantcontacten mag afhandelen.

Leertraject fase 2:

  • Na het succesvol afronden van fase 1 ga je ‘echt’ aan het werk. De nadruk in deze fase ligt op het verder ontwikkelen van je (sales) vaardigheden en gaat het tempo van klantcontact omhoog via outbound- en inbound belwerkzaamheden.
  • Je krijgt targets en gaat deelnemen aan performance dialogen met de andere stagiaires met als doel om van elkaar te leren. Een persoonlijke coach blijft je gedurende deze periode begeleiden.
  • Je krijg presentaties van collega’s die jou gaan uitleggen wat zij doen en gaat op locatie meekijken. Hiermee krijg je een beter beeld van mogelijke banen binnen ING.

Wat vraagt deze stage van je?

Je wilt graag tijd investeren in het verder ontwikkelen van jouw gespreksvaardigheden en je ervaring in klantcontact. Beleggen heeft je interesse, je bent een goede gesprekspartner en wilt klanten graag helpen bij het maken van de juiste keuzes. Je bent sales gedreven, resultaat gericht, neemt initiatief en kunt goed omgaan met feedback. Verder:

  • Je studeert aan een Hbo-opleiding en spreekt vloeiend Nederlands.
  • Je hebt WFT Basis in je bezit of bent bereid deze te halen voordat je bij ons start. Het liefst heb je ook WFT Vermogen en/of MiFID Informeren of ben je bereid deze te halen. Alle opleidingskosten worden vergoed door ING.
  • Je bent flexibel inzetbaar en combineert thuiswerken met werken vanuit één van de hub locaties Den Haag, Eindhoven, Leeuwarden, Zaandam en Zwolle of vanuit een ING-huis bij jou in de buurt.

Wat bieden wij?

  • Een meewerkstage vanaf februari 2027 afgestemd op de eisen vanuit jouw opleiding.
  • Een persoonlijke coach en leren onder werktijd.
  • Een uitdagende en leerzame omgeving met veel inzichten over mogelijke werkzaamheden binnen ING.
  • Een marktconforme stagevergoeding van EURO 700,- (bruto) bij een 36-urige werkweek.

Jouw sollicitatie

Stuur je CV voorzien van een motivatie waarin je uitlegt wie je bent, waarom jij de juiste kandidaat bent voor dit leertraject en op welke wijze je affiniteit met beleggen en/of de financiële markten hebt? Wij maken graag kennis met je.

Heb je vragen? Stuur dan een mail naar Bart Janssen, Digitaal Vermogen Team: Bart.Janssen1@ing.com.

title: D&T Project Manager (EPPM)
description:
Welcome to Haleon. We’re a purpose-driven, world-class consumer company putting everyday health in the hands of millions. In just three years since our launch, we’ve grown, evolved and are now entering an exciting new chapter – one filled with bold ambitions and enormous opportunity.

Our trusted portfolio of brands – including Sensodyne®, Panadol®, Advil®, Voltaren®, Theraflu®, Otrivin®, and Centrum® – lead in resilient and growing categories. What sets us apart is our unique blend of deep human understanding and trusted science.

Now it’s time to fully realise the full potential of our business and our people. We do this through our Win as One strategy. It puts our purpose – to deliver better everyday health with humanity – at the heart of everything we do. It unites us, inspires us, and challenges us to be better every day, driven by our agile, performance-focused culture.

About the role

The D&T Project Manager is responsible for the end‑to‑end delivery of technology projects within Haleon’s Digital & Technology (D&T) organisation.

The role ensures projects are delivered with discipline, transparency and predictability, operating within established delivery frameworks, governance standards and portfolio processes. Working closely with business stakeholders, delivery partners and cross‑functional D&T teams, the Project Manager maintains clear ownership of scope, plans, risks and outcomes.

This role is suited to an experienced delivery professional who is comfortable operating in structured, enterprise delivery environments, managing multiple stakeholders and suppliers, and providing clear, reliable insight throughout the project lifecycle.

Role purpose

To deliver D&T projects safely and predictably, ensuring agreed outcomes are achieved by applying standard delivery frameworks, managing risks and dependencies proactively, and maintaining clear communication with stakeholders and leadership.

Key accountabilities

  • The D&T Project Manager is accountable for:

  • Successful end‑to‑end delivery of assigned D&T projects

  • Consistent application of D&T delivery frameworks and governance

  • Effective management of scope, plans, risks, issues and dependencies

  • Clear, timely reporting of project status, risks and decisions

  • Strong stakeholder and supplier management

  • Maintaining focus on agreed business outcomes

Key responsibilities

1. Project Delivery & Execution

  • Own the delivery of assigned projects from initiation through to closure.

  • Ensure projects deliver agreed scope, timelines, quality standards and outcomes.

  • Apply standard D&T delivery approaches (Waterfall or hybrid as appropriate).

2. Planning & Control

  • Develop and maintain robust project plans, including milestones, dependencies and critical paths.

  • Track progress against plan and take corrective action where deviations occur.

  • Manage change in a controlled and transparent way.

3. Risk, Issue & Dependency Management

  • Proactively identify, manage and escalate project risks, issues and dependencies.

  • Ensure mitigation actions are clearly defined, owned and tracked to closure.

  • Maintain an accurate view of project health and delivery confidence at all times.

4. Stakeholder Management & Communication

  • Act as the primary point of contact for project stakeholders across business, D&T and suppliers.

  • Provide clear, honest and timely communication on progress, risks, decisions and impacts.

  • Manage expectations and maintain alignment throughout the project lifecycle.

5. Financial & Resource Management (Project Level)

  • Manage project budgets, forecasts and financial controls within delegated authority.

  • Work with Finance partners to provide accurate financial reporting and early visibility of variances.

  • Ensure project resources and capacity are planned and used effectively.

6. Supplier & Third‑Party Management

  • Manage delivery contributions from third‑party suppliers within the project scope.

  • Ensure suppliers deliver to agreed timelines, quality and contractual expectations.

  • Escalate supplier performance or dependency issues through appropriate governance forums.

7. Governance & Reporting

  • Operate within established delivery governance, ensuring all required artefacts and controls are maintained.

  • Provide accurate, decision‑oriented reporting into portfolio, performance and assurance forums.

  • Support reviews, stage gates and audits as required.

8. Outcomes, Adoption & Handover

  • Maintain focus on agreed business outcomes throughout delivery.

  • Support transition, handover and closure activities to enable successful adoption and ongoing ownership.

  • Contribute to benefits realisation tracking where applicable.

9. Continuous Improvement & Professional Standards

  • Apply lessons learned and best practice to improve delivery effectiveness.

  • Contribute positively to D&T delivery standards, ways of working and capability maturity.

  • Demonstrate accountability, professionalism and strong delivery discipline.

What good looks like

  • Projects are delivered with few surprises and clear delivery confidence

  • Risks and issues are identified early and managed proactively

  • Stakeholders have a clear understanding of progress, decisions and next steps

  • Delivery governance is followed consistently and professionally

  • Outcomes are achieved and transitions are well managed

The Federal Civilian Capture Director is responsible for leading, shaping, and winning strategic new business opportunities and re-compete efforts. This role drives all phases of complex capture efforts, integrating strategy, solution development, pricing, supply chain, and customer engagement to position the company for competitive advantage. The ideal candidate has extensive experience with large‑scale federal acquisitions, cross‑functional leadership, complex technical, and navigating long‑cycle, high‑visibility pursuits.

  • Identify and qualify new Federal Civilian opportunities aligned with corporate growth objectives.

  • Maintain deep awareness of market trends, competitive landscape, customer priorities, industrial base constraints, and government procurement processes.

Our work depends on a Membership Specialist joining our team to lead professionals supporting the Health Resources & Services Administration (HRSA).

The Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) aims to improve health outcomes by enhancing access to quality services, developing a skilled health workforce, and implementing innovative programs that benefit geographically isolated, economically or medically vulnerable populations. HRSA focuses on increasing health equity and strengthening local health systems through initiatives such as community health centers, the Organ Procurement & Transplantation Network (OPTN), the Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program, and support for maternal and child health.

The Membership Specialist plays a key role in supporting the integrity and effectiveness of Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) membership processes. This role involves monitoring compliance with OPTN policies and bylaws across transplant centers, organ procurement organizations (OPOs), and laboratories, as well as processing membership applications, maintaining accurate records, and performing data-driven analysis to enhance system quality.

The Membership Specialist acts as an essential liaison with members, providing guidance, ensuring regulatory adherence, and supporting the Membership and Professional Standards Committee (MPSC) in their oversight activities.

1. Application Review

  • Analyze membership applications and update requests for completeness, accuracy, and compliance standards.

  • Work with applicants to address deficiencies and ensure necessary documentation is submitted.

  • Prepare application summaries and support committees reviewing membership requests.

2. Analysis & Reporting

  • Perform quantitative and qualitative analysis of member performance metrics and trends.

  • Utilize dashboards and other documentation to support MPSC compliance reviews, performance improvement initiatives, and policy enforcement efforts.

  • Identify actionable insights and recommend improvements based on data analysis.

3. Stakeholder Communication

  • Respond promptly to inquiries from transplant centers, OPOs, and laboratories regarding membership applications, compliance, and policy-related questions.

  • Provide guidance and support to members navigating application and compliance processes.

4. Operational Support

  • Support MPSC activities, including member performance improvement and compliance reviews.

  • Maintain accurate records of applications, reviews, and membership data within OPTN tracking systems.

CSIG explores the interactions between users and industries to create innovative solutions for smart industries via technological advancements such as cloud, AI, and network security. While driving the digitalization of retail, medical, education, transportation and other industries, CSIG helps companies serve users in smarter ways, building a new ecosystem of intelligent industries that connect users and businesses.

What the Role Entails

PC Manager and Mobile Manager are among the most widely used utility apps in China, covering device cleaning, security protection, system optimization, and productivity tools. We are expanding our PC and mobile utility product portfolio into global markets and we are looking for a Senior Product Manager who can define where we play and how we win. You will own the product roadmap across multiple geographies, drive AI-powered feature innovation, and build the metrics framework that connects user experience to commercial outcomes. This role demands equal parts strategic thinking, hands-on execution, and comfort with ambiguity in emerging markets.
  • Own the product roadmap and release cycle for our global utility app portfolio, with direct accountability for user growth and revenue across Southeast Asia, LATAM, MENA, Europe, and North America.
  • Lead market and competitive research in key geographies — analyzing user needs, store and platform policies, and competitor positioning — to define market-entry and product differentiation strategies.
  • Drive AI integration across our utility product suite: identify high-impact use cases for LLMs, multimodal models, and on-device AI, scope the experience, and shepherd features from concept to launch.
  • Build and own the product measurement framework, using core metrics such as retention, conversion, and ARPU to make rigorous, data-driven decisions on both user experience and monetization.
  • Lead cross-functional execution — breaking complex, ambiguous problems into actionable plans, aligning engineering, design, marketing, and operations teams, and delivering measurable outcomes on tight iteration cycles.

Who We Look For

  • Bachelor's degree or above with 3+ years of consumer product management experience; prior experience with utility or tool apps is a strong plus.
  • Strong working knowledge of international markets with hands-on experience taking a product from 0 to 1, or scaling one through a high-growth phase in at least one overseas geography.
  • A pragmatic, execution-oriented understanding of AI capabilities, you can connect LLMs, multimodal models, and on-device inference to real product use cases and ship them.
  • Sharp analytical skills with the ability to independently go from raw data to insight to a shipped product change, using modern analytics and experimentation tooling.
  • Results-driven and comfortable with ambiguity — you test fast, learn fast, iterate fast, and have a proven ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders without formal authority.

Candidates should have a strong knowledge of circulation procedures and demonstrate an understanding of excellent customer service in a public library setting. Spanish speaking skills are preferred.

Entry level sales position capable of supporting the DIY business and achieve our sales and service objectives.   • Ability to work an assortment of days, evenings, and weekends as needed

Prior Experience that Sets a Salesperson up for Success

Physical Demands

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will predominantly be walking or standing. The employee is required to be able to talk and hear, and use hands and fingers to handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job, with or without reasonable accommodation. The employee is also occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts; high, precarious places; toxic or caustic chemicals; risk of electrical shock; explosives; and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Job Description

The Opportunity

Genpact is converting its G&A functions from process-efficient to agent-enabled. This is not incremental automation. It is a fundamental redesign of how work is structured, how roles are defined, and how the function operates when agents become co-workers.

This role owns that redesign - building the blueprint for what G&A functions look like post-agentic transition and ensuring that blueprint stays intact from design through to deployment.

What You Will Own

Process Redesign. Map end-to-end G&A processes, identify which tasks are candidates for agentic delegation, and define redesigned flows that reflect human-agent collaboration. This is rearchitecting from first principles - not layering automation onto existing processes.

Role Redesign. Define what human roles look like post-transition - which tasks are absorbed by agents, which require human judgment, and what new accountabilities emerge. The output is a coherent role architecture for a G&A function that runs differently, not just a list of tasks people will no longer perform.

Operating Model Design. Own the target operating model for an agentic G&A function - governance structure, decision rights, human-in-the-loop design principles, and the accountability framework that governs how agents are supervised, overridden, and continuously improved.

Governance Conduit. Serve as the structured interface between G&A function leaders, the AI CoE, and delivery teams. This is not coordination - it is design authority. Ensuring what gets built reflects what was designed, and that implementation decisions that deviate are escalated through the right governance channels before, not after, they cause drift.

What You Bring

  • Deep domain expertise across at least two G&A functions. You need to be credible in the room with a CFO, CHRO, and CPO simultaneously.
  • Demonstrated experience in process redesign and operating model transformation, ideally in a GBS or shared services context.
  • Sufficient literacy in agentic AI to be a meaningful conduit with AI CoE - not a builder, but someone who understands what agents can and cannot do, and where design intent typically breaks down in translation to build.
  • Structured thinking expressed through frameworks and blueprints. This role produces the design artefacts others build on.
  • The disposition to hold a line. In a matrixed environment with separate tech and delivery ownership, design intent erodes under execution pressure. This leader is the one who notices and acts.

title: Pricing Coordinator
description:
Pricing Coordinator

Location - Malaysia
Work Arrangement - Onsite

What we do at Weir
We are a global leader in mining technology for a sustainable future. We help our customers extract the resources the world needs more efficiently and more sustainably. Our planet’s future depends on the transition to renewable energy, and that transition can only happen with the metals and minerals our customers deliver. So, we work side by side with mines across the globe to move less rock, use less energy, use water wisely, and create less waste. Together, we drive the shift to smart, efficient, and more sustainable mining.

Make your impact
You’ll play a key role in solving real-world challenges. You’ll apply your skills to deliver results that matter whether that’s through engineering, planning or customer support. You’ll work with purpose, learn every day and help shape a more sustainable future.

What you’ll do

  • Pricing Data Analysis: Analyze pricing inputs from the executive team, apply logical pricing adjustments across customer and product combinations, and produce accurate pricing outputs daily. Success means delivering error-free pricing scenarios that support business margin goals.

  • Excel / Template Management: Maintain and validate pricing templates and formulas to ensure data integrity and accuracy, critical for reliable pricing decisions.

  • Salesforce Workflow Execution: Manage pricing workflows in Salesforce by tracking pricing review triggers, start/end dates, and task completions to ensure smooth pricing updates.

  • Coordination with Sales Team: Liaise with sales teams by creating and following up on pricing tasks, supporting the rollout of approved pricing changes without owning sales decisions.

  • Escalation & Deadline Management: Monitor timelines for pricing file completion, proactively escalate any delays or blockers, and ensure all pricing submissions are delivered on time.

  • Safety First: Demonstrate 100% commitment to our zero harm behaviors in support of our drive towards developing a world-class safety culture.

What you’ll bring


Must-haves:

  • Strong data analysis skills with attention to detail and accuracy

  • Proficiency in Excel and spreadsheet management

  • Ability to work with structured datasets and follow defined processes

  • Strong ownership of deadlines and proactive escalation skills

Nice-to-haves:

  • Experience with Salesforce for workflow tracking

  • Familiarity with SAP for data access and export

  • Exposure to pricing or commercial datasets

  • Comfortable working with clear instructions and structured tasks

Why join Weir?
We live our values we think safety first, do the right thing, respect each other, aim high, and delight our customers. We encourage our people to lead by example and celebrate our successes.


We’re passionate about our purpose to help deliver the natural resources that are essential to create a better future for the world. We do this by combining our deep customer insights, world-class engineering, materials science expertise, and intelligent automation to deliver innovative end-to-end solutions incorporating our signature technologies.
We believe your voice matters and your ideas make a difference. We’re working hard to nurture a diverse culture where our people feel like they belong and can do the best work of their lives. You can help shape our unique culture through our inclusion networks and safety initiatives.

Benefits

  • Competitive pay

  • Career development and learning support

  • Access to global inclusion networks

  • Regional and team-specific benefits

  • Sharebuilder scheme

  • Wellness support for you and your family

  • Collaboration with global teams

  • Study support

Founded in 1871, Weir is a world leading engineering business with a purpose to make mining operations smarter, more efficient and sustainable. Thanks to Weir’s technology, our customers can produce essential metals and minerals using less energy, water and waste at lower cost. With the increasing need for metals and minerals for climate change solutions, Weir colleagues are playing their part in powering a low carbon future. We are a global family of 11,000 uniquely talented people in over 60 countries, inspiring each other to do the best work of our lives.

For additional information about what it is like to work at Weir, please visit our Career Page and LinkedIn Life Page.

Weir is committed to an inclusive and diverse workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, veteran status, disability, age, or any other legally protected status.

Job Description:

GDIT has an immediate career opportunity for a Logistics Analyst Principal to join our Program Management Office (PMO) team at Aberdeen Proving Ground, MD.

Seize your opportunity to make a personal impact as a Procurement Operations Lead supporting our Worldwide Field Support (WFS) defense contract. GDIT is your place to make meaningful contributions to challenging projects while supporting critical Department of Defense missions around the globe.

At GDIT, people are our differentiators. As the Procurement Operations Lead (PMO), you will be responsible for leading procurement operations that directly enable worldwide logistics readiness and mission execution. Your work will ensure procurement activities are effectively integrated across Program Management, Supply Chain, Property Management, Engineering, Maintenance, Transportation, Finance, Contracts, and Government stakeholders while maintaining compliance with customer requirements and acquisition regulations.

HOW A LOGISTICS ANALYST PRINCIPAL WILL MAKE AN IMPACT

The Procurement Operations Lead serves as the operational owner of procurement activities across the Worldwide Field Support Program Management Office by leading procurement strategy, execution, integration, and continuous process improvement.


Responsibilities include:

  • Leads procurement operations supporting worldwide logistics requirements across multiple customer locations.
  • Serves as the primary procurement functional lead for the Program Management Office.
  • Owns the end-to-end procurement lifecycle from customer requirement through procurement closeout and invoice reconciliation.
  • Integrates procurement activities across Supply Chain Management, Property Management, Engineering, Maintenance, Transportation, Contracts, Finance, Strategic Acquisition Office (SAO), vendors, and Government customers.
  • Develops standardized procurement processes, procedures, and best practices to improve operational efficiency.
  • Independently leads procurement initiatives from planning through successful implementation with minimal supervision.
  • Establishes procurement priorities based on operational mission requirements while balancing competing customer demands.
  • Identifies procurement risks, develops mitigation strategies, and resolves issues before operational impacts occur.
  • Drives continuous improvement initiatives that reduce procurement cycle times, improve quality, and enhance customer support.
  • Develops, maintains, and improves procurement Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Desktop Procedures, and internal process documentation.
  • Tracks, analyzes, and reports procurement performance metrics while identifying opportunities for operational improvement.
  • Collaborates with leadership to develop procurement strategies supporting worldwide mission requirements.
  • Supports demand forecasting, strategic sourcing, vendor management, inventory optimization, cost reduction initiatives, and procurement planning.
  • Oversees procurement activities from Request for Quote (RFQ) through procurement, receipt, financial reconciliation, and closeout.
  • Ensures procurement actions comply with FAR, DFARS, company policies, customer requirements, and Strategic Acquisition Office procedures.
  • Maintains working knowledge of procurement payment methods, purchasing card reconciliation, vendor management, and procurement reporting.
  • Ensures accurate documentation and accountability supporting Government Furnished Property (GFP) and Contract Acquired Property (CAP) throughout the procurement lifecycle.
  • Maintains knowledge of PIEE and associated Government property accountability processes.
  • Maintains working knowledge of CHESS, FEDLOG, FEDMall, AESIP, IGC, TMDE, Trade Compliance, and other Government logistics systems supporting procurement operations.
  • Develops meaningful procurement dashboards, operational metrics, and executive reports supporting informed decision-making.
  • Conducts internal assessments, identifies process deficiencies, performs root cause analysis, and implements corrective actions.
  • Leads a small procurement team by establishing priorities, mentoring personnel, promoting accountability, and fostering professional development.
  • Builds collaborative relationships across the PMO to ensure procurement activities remain synchronized with overall logistics operations.
  • Communicates effectively with Government customers, vendors, senior leadership, and internal stakeholders both verbally and in writing.
  • Supports fast-paced worldwide operations while effectively managing multiple priorities and short suspense requirements.
  • Demonstrates initiative by taking ownership of complex projects and driving them to successful completion.


WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO SUCCEED


Education


Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, or a related discipline; equivalent experience may be substituted.


Required Experience

  • Eight (8) or more years of progressively responsible experience in procurement, logistics, supply chain management, acquisition, or program operations.
  • Experience leading procurement operations supporting Department of Defense programs.
  • Demonstrated experience developing procurement processes and leading operational improvements.
  • Experience integrating procurement activities across multiple functional organizations.
  • Experience leading projects independently from planning through implementation.

Required Skills and Abilities

  • Strong leadership and organizational skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to think strategically while executing tactically.
  • Proven process improvement mindset.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to influence cross-functional teams without direct authority.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced operational environment.
  • Strong understanding of FAR, DFARS, Government procurement, and supply chain principles.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience supporting Worldwide Field Support or similar global logistics operations.
  • Knowledge of Government Furnished Property (GFP) accountability.
  • Experience with PIEE, CHESS, FEDLOG, FEDMall, AESIP, IGC, and TMDE.
  • Knowledge of Statement of Work (SOW), Bill of Materials (BOM), Sole Source Justifications (SSJ), Return Material Authorization (RMA), and Strategic Acquisition Office processes.
  • Knowledge of invoice schedule and payment terms.
  • Lean Six Sigma, PMP, or other process improvement/project management certification is desirable.

Security Clearance

title: Pathology Director
description:
Job Title: Director of Pathology

Location: Cambridge, UK

Hybrid working: Minimum 3 days per week in the office

Introduction to role:

Are you ready to bring decisive medical leadership in pathology to accelerate personalised diagnostics that guide clinical trials and patient care? This is a chance to shape how novel biomarkers become trusted tests that identify the right patients for the right therapies, faster.

You will join our internal accredited laboratory delivering in-house diagnostic testing for early-phase clinical studies and pioneering approaches in patient stratification. Your oversight will ensure assays are robust, validated and clinically meaningful, directly influencing how our medicines are developed and how patients are selected for studies. Working at the intersection of pathology, quality, and translational science, you will help advance companion and complementary diagnostics— including computational pathology and image analysis—across a biomarker-driven portfolio.

At Director level, you will look beyond daily operations to set direction, influence governance, and represent the laboratory in internal and external forums. Will you help us lift diagnostic standards, bring new technologies into practice, and translate cutting-edge science into results that clinicians and patients can trust?

Accountabilities:

- Medical and Technical Oversight: Provide pathology oversight of assay performance, result review and reporting practices in an accredited environment supporting clinical and biomarker development.

- CAP/CLIA and GxP Compliance: Act in a role aligned to CAP/CLIA expectations; ensure testing and reporting practices meet regulatory and professional standards, including ISO 15189, GCP, IVDR and HTA requirements.

- Result Authorisation and Interpretation: Review, interpret and approve laboratory results and reports, ensuring outputs are scientifically valid, clinically appropriate and compliant with defined quality requirements; contribute to clinical and scientific interpretation of pathology and biomarker data.

- Method Evaluation and Approval: As technical lead, evaluate and approve novel test methods; ensure fitness for purpose and appropriate validation or verification before clinical use.

- Operational Partnership: Work closely with the Laboratory Director, QA/QC and operational leadership to evolve methods, procedures, instrumentation, staffing models and workflow design.

- Strategy and Companion Diagnostics: Provide scientific and medical input into assay and biomarker strategy, including companion diagnostic development and clinical implementation planning; align with broader clinical development objectives.

- Innovation and Digital Pathology: Drive continuous improvement and the introduction of emerging technologies, including digital pathology, image analysis and data-enabled diagnostic workflows.

- Clinical Trial Support: Provide medical and technical oversight for prospective patient testing in clinical studies, ensuring protocol-aligned reporting, documentation and quality standards.

- External Engagement and Governance: Represent the laboratory in governance forums; contribute to external regulatory interactions; lead capability-building in diagnostic pathology and companion diagnostics across matrix teams.

Essential Skills/Experience:

- Medical degree recognised by the General Medical Council (GMC). - Current Licence to Practice in the United Kingdom.

- Significant experience practising at consultant pathologist level, or equivalent senior medical pathology role, within a diagnostic or regulated laboratory environment.

- Experience providing medical and technical oversight for testing within an accredited or regulated laboratory environment.

- Strong working knowledge of CAP/CLIA, ISO 15189, GCP, IVDR, HTA and applicable standards governing laboratory quality systems, patient testing, and report issuance.

- Experience reviewing, authorising, or providing medical oversight of laboratory reports, ensuring outputs are scientifically valid, medically appropriate, and compliant with regulatory and quality requirements.

- Ability to provide clear clinical and scientific interpretation of pathology and biomarker data, integrating findings with other data streams where relevant.

- Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work effectively across matrix teams and provide oversight to multidisciplinary laboratory activities.

Desirable Skills/Experience:

- GMC Specialist Registration in an appropriate pathology specialty.

- FRCPath in Histopathology or another relevant pathology discipline, or equivalent specialist qualification.

- PhD, MD(Res), or equivalent higher research qualification in pathology, oncology, translational medicine, biomarker science, or a related discipline.

- Experience in companion diagnostic and predictive biomarker development within pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or accredited diagnostic laboratory settings, working in line with ISO 13485 and ISO 14971.

- Experience serving in a role aligned to CAP Technical Supervisor, General Supervisor, or Laboratory Director responsibilities for high-complexity testing.

- Familiarity with digital pathology, image analysis, and computational pathology approaches in a regulated environment.

- Experience with diagnostic methods, such as PCR, NGS, spatial omics, proteomics, mass spectrometry and other platforms relevant to precision medicine.

- Experience leading or supporting clinical trial assay governance, including oversight of testing strategies, report processes, and protocol-aligned patient testing.

- Experience overseeing or contributing to prospective patient testing in support of clinical trials, including understanding of protocol-driven testing, result reporting, and documentation requirements.

When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. In-person working gives us the platform we need to connect, work at pace and challenge perceptions. That's why we work, on average, a minimum of three days per week from the office. But that doesn't mean we're not flexible. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual flexibility. Join us in our unique and ambitious world.

Why AstraZeneca:

Here, your expertise in diagnostic pathology fuels a bold mission: detecting disease earlier, matching patients to targeted treatments and tackling some of the toughest cancers through science and technology. With a deep, well-funded pipeline and teams empowered to make smart, fast decisions, we bring clinicians, data scientists and engineers together to turn breakthrough ideas into validated tests that shape studies and patient outcomes. You will find the ambition to push boundaries balanced with a culture that values collaboration and kindness—so you can lead, learn and see the real-world impact of your work every day.

Lead the evolution of diagnostics that guide life-changing medicines—take the next step in your career and shape how patients are identified and treated.

title: Senior Information Security Engineer
description:

Wells Fargo is seeking a Senior Information Security Engineer


In this role, you will:

  • Lead or participate in computer security incident response activities for moderately complex events

title: Senior Engineer - TV Operation
description:
Join our Team

About this opportunity:

This opportunity offers a key Technical Authority (2nd Level Assurance) role within a 24×7 TV Network Management Centre (TVNMC). The role is responsible for ensuring high availability and SLA compliance across live broadcast, on‑deamand, interactive TV, and media application services. You will handle complex incidents beyond front‑office support, working with Linear Broadcast, IPTV/OTT platforms, VOD systems, middleware, interactive services, and media delivery applications. It provides strong exposure to end‑to‑end media workflows while collaborating with cross‑functional teams, vendors, and partners—ideal for engineers seeking technical ownership and growth in customer‑facing, mission‑critical media operations.

What you will do:

Take full ownership of reactive maintenance activities beyond Front Office (L1 monitoring), ensuring faults are diagnosed and resolved with minimal service impact.
Ensure ongoing SLA/WLA compliance and maintain the highest levels of service availability for customers.
Lead incident handling, fault diagnosis, service restoration, and Root Cause Analysis (RCA) to drive permanent fault resolution.
Manage and resolve escalated tickets with accountability, ensuring timely updates and closure within defined SLA windows.
Engage directly with customers, providing clear technical communication and maintaining a customer-first approach throughout every interaction.
Influence and guide NOC teams, vendors, and internal stakeholders toward effective and timely fault resolution.

The skills you bring:

Education: Degree in Electronics & Telecommunication, Telecom Engineering, or an equivalent discipline.
Experience: 5–10 years of hands-on experience in Telecom or Media Delivery environments.
Strong customer-facing communication skills with the ability to manage expectations and deliver results under pressure.
Proven track record in 2nd Level support, troubleshooting, ticket handling, escalation management, and RCA.
Broadcast-Centric Expertise
Deep understanding of live broadcast signal flow, including IRD, Encoders, Transcoders, Broadcast Gateways, MPEG-2/4 Transport Streams, Multicast IP, Multiplexers, Remux, and Modulators.
Hands-on experience with RF and Satellite systems, including IF/RF infrastructure, L-Band routers, splitters, C/Ku band dishes, link budget calculations, frequency planning, and symbol rate management.
Working knowledge of OTT platforms, including headend design, Middleware, CDN, DRM, and OTT streaming protocols such as DASH, HLS, Smooth, and HDS.
Familiarity with EMS/NMS monitoring tools for platform performance and alarm management.
Experience with Compliance Recording systems and processes.
Understanding of Interactive Services including Red Button Services, FAST Channels, and Mosaic Services.
Hands-on experience with IPTV platforms, covering rolling stream servers, performance and software management via NMS, content distribution via CDN, and Replay TV service
VOD & Content-Centric Expertise
Strong knowledge of the VOD ecosystem, including Catch-up TV, progressive download, and deferred live services.
Experience managing VOD ingestion pipelines and Content Management Systems (CMS).
Familiarity with playback and storage infrastructure, including live content storage servers and ADC servers.
Understanding of VOD Advanced Advertising solutions, including manifest delivery and control mechanisms.
Experience with media delivery applications, including application integration and media content publishing workflows.
Multi-vendor expertise across VOD and content delivery platforms.

All academic credentials must be from recognized and accredited institutions and are further subject to verification.

title: Change Enablement Specialist – Global IT
description:
Make an impact with NTT DATA
Join a company that is pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We are renowned for our technical excellence and leading innovations, and for making a difference to our clients and society. Our workplace embraces diversity and inclusion – it’s a place where you can grow, belong and thrive.

Your day at NTT DATA

The Change Enablement Specialist is a subject matter expert in change management, responsible for strengthening and evolving the Change Enablement capability across Global IT. The role designs, delivers and continuously improves digital and blended learning solutions that build practical change capability and address skills gaps across IT programmes, regional change teams and change networks.

Working closely with Change Leads, Regional Change Managers and transformation teams, the Change Enablement Specialist ensures our Change Management framework, tools and learning interventions translate into effective implementation, stronger adoption and measurable business outcomes.

The role combines change management expertise, learning and capability development, and data-driven continuous improvement to help build a consistent, scalable and industry-leading approach to Change Enablement.

Key Responsibilities

1. Change Management Subject Matter Expertise

  • Act as a Change Management SME, providing practical expertise, guidance and recommendations to Change Leads, Regional Change Managers and programme teams.
  • Demonstrate strong understanding of the Global IT Change Management approach, framework, methodologies and tools, supporting their consistent and effective application.
  • Identify opportunities to improve change management practices based on business needs, programme experience, emerging trends and best practice.
  • Anticipate evolving transformation and adoption needs and recommend new approaches, tools and interventions to strengthen Change Enablement effectiveness.

2. Change Capability & Learning

  • Design, develop and deliver digital, virtual and blended learning solutions that build change management capability across the organisation.
  • Identify capability gaps and translate them into practical learning journeys, resources, toolkits and interventions.
  • Develop learning that enables people to apply change management effectively in real transformation scenarios, rather than focusing solely on theoretical knowledge.
  • Own and evolve Change Enablement learning content to ensure it remains relevant, practical and aligned with the needs of the business.

3. Regional & Change Network Capability

  • Partner with Regional Change Managers to strengthen the capability of regional Change Networks and support effective local delivery and adoption.
  • Develop scalable learning and enablement programmes for Change Makers, Change Agents, Business Champions and other change communities.
  • Provide Regional Change Managers with tools, materials and guidance that can be adapted to regional and business needs.
  • Help create an active community of change practitioners that shares knowledge, experience and best practice across the organisation.

4. Measurement & Continuous Improvement

  • Define and monitor measures to evaluate the effectiveness of learning and capability interventions.
  • Use data, adoption insights, participant feedback and programme outcomes to assess impact on engagement, readiness, adoption and business value.
  • Establish feedback loops that turn lessons learned from programmes and regional teams into improvements to frameworks, learning and tools.
  • Experiment with new approaches and technologies to improve how change capability is developed and scaled.
  • Provide actionable insights and recommendations to the Change Enablement team based on evidence and emerging needs.

5. Innovation & Future Capability

  • Foster a culture of curiosity, experimentation and continuous learning across the Change Enablement community.
  • Monitor emerging change management practices, digital learning approaches and technology trends, including AI-enabled opportunities.
  • Translate relevant external best practice into practical improvements for the Global IT Change Enablement approach.
  • Contribute to building a consistent, scalable and industry-leading enterprise change capability that supports successful IT transformation.

What You'll Bring - Skills & Attributes

  • Strong expertise in organisational change management and practical application of change methodologies.
  • Experience designing and delivering learning, capability-building or practitioner development programmes.
  • Strong understanding of stakeholder engagement, business readiness, adoption and behavioural change.
  • Ability to translate complex change concepts into simple, practical and engaging learning experiences.
  • Analytical mindset and confidence using data and feedback to evaluate effectiveness and drive improvement.
  • Strong facilitation, communication, coaching and stakeholder management skills.
  • Curious and innovative mindset, with a willingness to experiment and challenge established approaches.
  • Ability to operate effectively across a complex, global and matrixed organisation.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Proven experience in Change Management, Change Enablement, Organisational Development or a related field.
  • Practical experience supporting large-scale technology or business transformation.
  • Experience designing digital, virtual and/or blended learning solutions.
  • Experience developing change capability across distributed teams, communities or change networks.
  • Experience measuring learning effectiveness, adoption or change outcomes.
  • Prosci, APMG Change Management or equivalent change management qualification preferred.

Success Measures

Success in this role will be demonstrated through:

  • Increased change management capability across IT programmes, regions and Change Networks.
  • High-quality, scalable learning interventions that translate into practical application.
  • Measurable improvement in change readiness, engagement and adoption outcomes.
  • Increased consistency and effectiveness in the application of the Global IT Change Management framework.
  • Strong partnership with Regional Change Managers and effective support for their Change Networks.
  • Evidence-based improvements to Change Enablement tools, learning and methodologies.
  • A growing culture of curiosity, experimentation, knowledge sharing and continuous improvement across the Change Enablement community.

title: Director, Environmental Compliance
description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

Title: Director, Environmental Compliance

Location: Alpharetta, GA; Columbus, OH; Dallas, TX (REQUIRED)

Remote/Hybrid/Onsite: Hybrid Role

The Role:

The Director, Environmental Compliance leads enterprise-wide environmental programs, ensuring regulatory alignment, operational excellence, cross-functional collaboration, and continuous improvement. This role provides strategic direction for hazardous materials and waste management, product onboarding protocols, environmental compliance planning, and reporting across all business units. Essential duties and responsibilities include:

  • Provide strategic direction and oversight for the environmental compliance team, fostering a culture of excellence and continuous improvement.
  • Develop and monitor key compliance metrics, analytics and audit criteria to assess program effectiveness and ensure regulatory alignment.
  • Lead collaboration with third party vendors, master data teams and compliance partners to ensure accuracy and accessibility of Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and hazardous materials classification data.
  • Maintain and develop subject matter expertise in hazardous waste (EPA/state), hazardous materials shipping (49 CFR, IATA, IMDG), and storage (NFPA, IFC) regulations.
  • Lead the development and governance of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), training programs, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Provide oversight of hazardous waste disposal vendor performance, problem resolution, and achievement of key performance indicators.
  • Direct development of air and water pollution prevention plans, including permit acquisition and implementation of compliance monitoring systems.
  • Oversee federal and state-level hazardous materials spill control plans and reporting, including Biennial Reporting, Hazardous Materials Business Plan (HMBP), and Tier II submissions.
  • Manage regulatory inspections and enforcement actions in conjunction with business partners and legal counsel.
  • Lead proactive compliance strategies in response to emerging federal and state regulations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the creation and improvement of environmental policies and programs to ensure regulatory compliance across the enterprise. (40%)
  • Guide and support the environmental compliance team in setting goals, managing risks, and developing training and coaching initiatives. (30%)
  • Drive innovation in systems to track and improve environmental compliance through data and analytics. (20%)
  • Function as the environmental subject matter expert for company-wide initiatives and emergencies involving environmental compliance risks. (10%)

Qualifications

Critical Skills and Experience

  • Demonstrate at least 10 years of progressive experience in environmental compliance, preferably within distribution and warehousing environments.
  • Possess expertise in designing and managing regulatory compliance programs for hazardous materials transportation and hazardous waste management.
  • Exhibit exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey complex topics clearly and succinctly to diverse audiences.
  • Demonstrate advanced organizational, analytical, and critical thinking skills to evaluate information, identify key issues, and drive effective resolutions.
  • Lead cross-functional teams and independently manage multiple priorities with a collaborative and proactive approach.
  • Basic computer skills, including familiarity with internet, email, and business application programs, and AI technology.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Typically requires 12+ years of professional experience and 4+ years of management experience.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience preferred.
  • Professional certifications such as Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM) preferred.

Physical Requirements

  • General office demands
  • Must have the ability to travel up to 20% of the time

Must be authorized to work in the US. Sponsorship is not available for this position.

title: Senior Desktop Engineer
description:

Desktop & Endpoint Engineering

Connectivity, Mobility & VDI (Endpoint Side)

Endpoint Security – Hands & Feet

CMDB & Documentation
